sites.name: East 55th / Woodland / Kinsman
sites.connection: Save-Way and Cleveland Trust signs, together with the street layout, connect these early exterior shots to this junction. Pin marks the junction; the camera position remains approximate.
sites.history: City records place the Cleveland Trust branch at 5424 Woodland, built in 1924 and now demolished. A library directory places Save-Way at 5307 Woodland.

sites.name: Western Reserve Building / Superior Hill
sites.connection: Distinctive bay windows and the Terminal Tower view match the downhill exterior during the final pursuit. Pin locates the landmark, not the precise camera position.
sites.history: Built in 1891–92 for Samuel Mather, the Western Reserve Building was designed by Burnham & Root and housed iron and shipping businesses.

sites.name: Detroit–Superior Bridge
sites.connection: Concrete approach arches and the lower streetcar deck are visible during the final pursuit. Other river shots show its central steel arch in the background.
sites.history: Opened in 1917, the bridge carried road traffic above and streetcars below. It is now officially the Veterans Memorial Bridge.

sites.name: B&O Railroad Bridge No. 463 / Powerhouse
sites.address: Flats, near Sycamore Street and the Powerhouse
sites.connection: The raised bascule bridge, Powerhouse and Detroit–Superior arch form a distinctive alignment in the film’s final river sequence.
sites.history: The mid-1950s railroad bridge survives beside the former streetcar Powerhouse. Its raised span makes it a useful landmark for reconstructing the film’s views.

sites.name: Carter Road Lift Bridge
sites.address: Carter Road over the Cuyahoga River
sites.connection: Lift towers and an adjacent railroad crossing resemble Carter Road. This is a provisional visual identification; a matching historical camera angle is still needed.
sites.history: The 1940 vertical-lift bridge is documented in the Library of Congress engineering survey HAER OH-56.
sources: Library of Congress survey and photographs

sites.name: West 3rd Street Lift Bridge
sites.address: West 3rd Street over the Cuyahoga River
sites.connection: The red through-truss lift span, vehicles and industrial backdrop suggest West 3rd Street. The bridge and the steelworks identification remain provisional.
sites.history: The vertical-lift span dates from 1940. Later rehabilitation changed its appearance, so period photographs are more useful than current views.

sites.name: Superior Hill hotel / possible Bethel House
sites.connection: The film’s hotel exterior appears near Superior Hill and the B&O bridge. Bethel House is an address-based candidate; neither its façade nor its 1968 name has been confirmed. Hotel interiors are not established as the same building.
sites.history: The city’s architectural inventory lists Bethel House Hotel at 1468 West 10th, built in 1890–91 and demolished. Pin is an approximate street-range location, not a verified film site.

sites.name: United Electric storefront — unplaced
sites.address: Historical address leads: 1772 East 9th Street; 5805 Euclid Avenue
sites.connection: The film sign reads United Electric Supply / Lighting Fixtures. Two similarly named Cleveland companies make the sign alone insufficient to choose a site. No point is plotted.
sites.history: A 1956 court record distinguishes United Electric Fixture & Supply at 1772 East 9th from United Electric Supply at 5805 Euclid. These are research leads, not confirmed shooting addresses.

sites.name: Leader Drug street scene — unplaced
sites.connection: Leader Drug is readable across the street gathering. The chain had multiple branches; the film image has not been matched to a particular Cleveland address. No point is plotted.
sites.history: Leader Drug was part of Cleveland’s pharmacy industry. The chain’s history provides context but does not identify this branch or establish the scene’s exact city.

sites.name: Final steelworks / ore yard — unplaced
sites.address: Industrial-valley lead; plant and parcel unknown
sites.connection: Ore piles and a large bucket gantry appear in the final sequence. The precise plant, property and camera position are not established, so no point is plotted.
sites.history: The surrounding river sequence connects to Cleveland’s industrial Flats. That context does not prove a particular steel company owned the filmed yard.
